name: Multimodal stereo decoding and losses: ADL + dominant-modal estimator (DME), SMD-Nets, Stereo Risk (L1 risk), top-k soft-argmax (CoEx), single-modal weighted average (SMWA, Chen 2019)
authors_org: ADL/DME: Peng Xu, Zhiyu Xiang, Chengyu Qiao, Jingyun Fu, Tianyu Pu (Zhejiang University). SMD-Nets: Fabio Tosi, Yiyi Liao, Carolin Schmitt, Andreas Geiger (Univ. Bologna / MPI-IS / Tuebingen). Stereo Risk: Ce Liu, Suryansh Kumar, Shuhang Gu, Radu Timofte, Yao Yao, Luc Van Gool (ETH Zurich and others). CoEx top-k: Antyanta Bangunharcana et al. (KAIST). SMWA: Chuangrong Chen, Xiaozhi Chen, Hui Cheng (Sun Yat-sen Univ. / DJI).
year: SMWA 2019 (ICCV); SMD-Nets 2021 (CVPR); CoEx 2021 (IROS); ADL 2024 (CVPR; arXiv 2023); Stereo Risk 2024 (ICML)
venue_link: ADL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.15612 , CVPR 2024 https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2024/papers/Xu_Adaptive_Multi-Modal_Cross-Entropy_Loss_for_Stereo_Matching_CVPR_2024_paper.pdf ; SMD-Nets: https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021/papers/Tosi_SMD-Nets_Stereo_Mixture_Density_Networks_CVPR_2021_paper.pdf , https://autonomousvision.github.io/smdnets/ ; Stereo Risk: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.03152 , PMLR 235:31326-31343 https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/liu24af.html ; CoEx: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.05773 , https://github.com/antabangun/coex ; SMWA: https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_ICCV_2019/html/Chen_On_the_Over-Smoothing_Problem_of_CNN_Based_Disparity_Estimation_ICCV_2019_paper.html
code_availability: ADL: https://github.com/xxxupeng/ADL . SMD-Nets: https://github.com/fabiotosi92/SMD-Nets . CoEx: https://github.com/antabangun/coex . SMWA: https://github.com/chenchr/otosp . Stereo Risk: [uncertain] no official repository found in this search. All decoders are a few lines of tensor code and can be applied to our saved posteriors without the repos.
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed (ICCV/CVPR/ICML/IROS), plus an in-house measurement: every decode family in this item was evaluated on the saved ConvNeXt posteriors for all 155 holdout wells (results/baseline_check_posterior_all/posterior_all.npz, 23,634 posterior columns, 60-epoch 0801_V2 baseline) with scratchpad scripts decode_probe.py and decode_probe2.py. The in-house numbers are single-model diagnostics, not trained ablations.
extreme_summary: Stereo papers fix the 'soft-argmin blends two modes' problem with mode-seeking decodes: pick the dominant mode (DME, SMWA, SMD-Nets), keep only the top-k bins (CoEx), or use the median via L1 risk (Stereo Risk). All of these optimise EPE, bad-pixel rate or edge sharpness, not squared error. On our posteriors every one of them raises pooled RMSE, from 5.48 ft (mean) to 5.52-6.28 ft. Stereo Risk proves the expectation is the L2-risk minimiser, which is exactly our metric, so the transferable parts are the training losses and calibration, not the decoders.
task_definition: Per-pixel disparity from a stereo cost volume whose per-pixel distribution is multimodal at object edges (foreground vs background) or in repetitive texture. Mapping to Erudition: the per-MD-column softmax over 400 TVT levels, which is multimodal when repeated rock bands match the GR (about 16% of rows are multimodal in the dump).
inputs: Stereo cost volumes (PSMNet, GwcNet, GANet, IGEV backbones). For us: the 16-channel 345 x 400 cost image and the U-Net's alignment_logits.
target_parameterisation: Discrete disparity bins with a distribution over them (ADL, SMWA, CoEx, Stereo Risk), or a continuous bimodal Laplacian mixture (mu1, b1, mu2, b2, pi) per pixel (SMD-Nets). Ours: TVT - TVT0 in 400 half-foot levels (-99.75 to 99.75 ft).
output_representation: A per-pixel distribution in every case, turned into a point estimate by the decoder. SMD-Nets outputs a 2-component mixture, which could feed a K-hypothesis reranker (see B04).
architecture: Loss and decoder changes on standard cost-volume networks; the backbones are unchanged. ADL: multimodal ground truth built per pixel by DBSCAN clustering (eps = 3 px) of ground-truth disparities in an m x n local window, turned into a Laplacian mixture (b = 0.8). The centre pixel's own cluster gets weight at least alpha = 0.5, and the rest is split by cluster size. SMD-Nets: any 2D/3D stereo backbone plus a continuous MLP head that predicts bimodal Laplacian parameters at arbitrary sub-pixel query locations. CoEx: guided cost-volume excitation, then top-k (e.g. k = 2) selection before soft-argmin. Stereo Risk: IGEV-style backbone with Laplacian-kernel interpolation of the discrete distribution into a continuous density; the output is the L1-risk minimiser (the median) found by binary search, and gradients come from the implicit function theorem.
core_mechanism: The shared diagnosis: soft-argmin is the mean of the distribution, and on a bimodal distribution the mean lands between modes where no true surface exists. The cures fall into three groups. (1) Decode only one mode: DME splits the distribution into modes, picks the one with the largest cumulative mass (not the tallest peak, which is noise-sensitive), then takes soft-argmax inside it. SMWA takes the mode around the argmax and averages within its monotone flanks. SMD-Nets picks the mixture component with the highest density [uncertain on the exact selection formula]. (2) Truncate: CoEx top-k soft-argmin uses only the k largest bins. (3) Change the risk: Stereo Risk shows the expectation is the L2-risk minimiser and that the L1 minimiser (median) is more robust on multimodal pixels under EPE. On the training side, ADL and SMWA both find that cross-entropy against a smoothed target beats L1 regression on the soft-argmin output. ADL goes further and lets the target itself be multimodal where the local ground-truth structure is multimodal.
training_objective: ADL: cross-entropy against the adaptive multimodal Laplacian-mixture target. SMWA: cross-entropy against a Gaussian-smoothed one-hot target (variance 2), better than L1. SMD-Nets: negative log-likelihood of the bimodal Laplacian mixture. Stereo Risk: L1 loss on the risk-minimiser output, trained end-to-end through the implicit function theorem; L1 risk at both training and test time works best, test-time-only gives marginal gains. CoEx: smooth-L1 on the top-k soft-argmin. Ours today (experiments/arch/seq_NN_cfg.py): alignment cross-entropy to an 'exp_smooth' Gaussian target with sigma 1.25 levels (weight 0.05*4/3), plus Huber (delta 1.0) regression on the expectation (weight 0.05/3), plus a GR penalty (0.05/3). A distance-aware ranked-probability loss ('CDF', masked_typewell_cdf_loss, squared difference of predicted and target CDFs) is implemented but set to weight 0.0.
decoding: DME: mode split, then the mode with maximum cumulative probability, then soft-argmax restricted to that mode. SMWA: argmax peak, monotone-descent bounds, local weighted mean. SMD-Nets: mean of the dominant mixture component. CoEx: soft-argmin over the top-k bins. Stereo Risk: median of the Laplacian-interpolated continuous density. Erudition: full expectation over 400 levels (the model prediction equals the posterior mean to 9e-6 ft).
metric_consistent_decode: All the stereo decoders here are mode-seeking or median (L1) decoders, not Bayes-optimal for RMSE. Measured on our 155-well posteriors (23,634 columns): mean 5.480 ft; median / L1 risk 5.636; SMWA 6.282; argmax 6.274; posterior_analysis 'dominant_mode' (DME-like) 6.061 at row level; top-k k = 2/4/8/16/32/64 gives 6.226/6.117/5.946/5.697/5.548/5.517. Temperature sharpening p^(1/T): T = 0.5 5.583, 0.7 5.500, 0.85 5.478, 1.0 5.480, 1.2 5.507, 1.5 5.586, 2.0 5.795. The global temperature optimum is flat around 0.85-1.0, a gain of 0.001 ft. The mean decode is confirmed as the right choice.
evidence_scope: Per-pixel decoders using local context only (ADL's target uses a local window). No whole-scene or multi-image evidence. In our terms: a single MD column's posterior.
prefix_conditioning: None. Stereo has no labelled prefix. Mode choice could in principle be conditioned on the known heel TVT, but that is continuity or prefix evidence (B05/B10), not a decode trick. The post-hoc forward-backward continuity decode has already failed.
propose_vs_select: Selection at decode time: pick one mode out of the distribution. SMD-Nets' 2-component head is a natural proposal generator (two hypotheses plus weights) that a downstream reranker or gate could select from. That is the B04 path, and the oracle best-mode decode (4.27 ft) bounds its value.
physical_constraints: None beyond per-pixel unimodality assumptions (SMWA, DME) or bimodality (SMD-Nets). ADL's multimodal target encodes the fact that edges straddle two surfaces.
dataset: SceneFlow (synthetic), KITTI 2012/2015, Middlebury, ETH3D; SMD-Nets adds its own 4K synthetic UnrealStereo4K dataset.
synthetic_to_real: ADL and Stereo Risk report better synthetic-to-real generalisation: ADL on KITTI after SceneFlow pretraining; Stereo Risk on Middlebury, 12.63% against 13.76% bad-pixel when trained only on synthetic data. No calibration transfer analysis.
metric_and_performance: ADL (SceneFlow): PSMNet EPE 0.97 to 0.78 with ADL + DME (>1px 10.51% to 6.30%, >3px 4.03% to 2.71%); GwcNet + ADL + DME EPE 0.62. Ablation on PSMNet: unimodal loss + SME 0.84, unimodal + DME 0.82, multimodal + SME 0.80, multimodal + DME 0.78. So the loss contributes more than the decoder. KITTI-15 D1-all: PSMNet 2.14% to 1.59%; GANet + ADL 1.40%; KITTI-12 GANet + ADL 1.29%, ranked first. Stereo Risk (SceneFlow, IGEV base): >1px 5.21% to 4.22%, >0.5px 8.51% to 8.10%; runtime 0.17 to 0.25 s on an RTX 3090; 11.96M parameters. SMWA: gains reported on its soft-edge-error metric; its authors accept minor boundary misalignment. SMD-Nets: sharper boundaries and better soft-edge error. [uncertain] SMD-Nets headline numbers were not retrieved. None of the papers reports RMSE.
comparability: Not comparable. The stereo metrics are EPE (a mean absolute error, where median-like decodes help) and bad-pixel rates (0/1 losses, where mode decodes help). Our metric is pooled RMSE, for which the conditional mean is optimal. The in-house decode sweep is directly comparable: the same 155 holdout wells, but at posterior-column rather than row resolution (mean 5.480 on columns against 5.474 at row level).
validation_protocol: Standard benchmark splits and servers. For our in-house probe, temperature and top-k were swept on the holdout itself (in-sample), which can only flatter the alternatives, and they still lost.
inference_budget: Negligible for all decoders (per-column operations over 400 levels). Stereo Risk's binary search added about 50% runtime in stereo. For us, any of these costs well under 1 ms per well.
repeated_layers: This is the item's central relevance: repeated bands produce exactly the multimodal per-column posterior these papers target. The evidence says mode-seeking is wrong for our metric. In the dump, band-related categories are wrong_mode 24%, blend 15% and multimodal_miss 12% of SSE. DME-style mode picking turns 'blend' rows (the mean sits between the modes) into 'wrong_mode' rows whenever the dominant mode is wrong. Because the model's dominant mode is wrong often enough, pooled RMSE rises from 5.47 to 6.06. The oracle best-mode decode (4.27 ft) shows the prize exists but can only be claimed with new evidence that identifies the right mode, not with a decoding rule.
drift: Not addressed by any of these methods. The low-spread group in our dump (posterior sd below 3.4 ft, half the columns) is overconfident: mean predicted variance 5.5 ft^2 against an actual MSE of 9.3 ft^2. That is the drift/offset signature (a unimodal hump centred slightly wrong), and no decode fixes a displaced unimodal hump.
uncertainty_and_calibration: SMD-Nets gives explicit aleatoric uncertainty through its mixture. ADL, Stereo Risk and CoEx do not evaluate calibration. In-house calibration read-out (decode_probe.py / decode_probe2.py): central-interval coverage is 0.586 at the nominal 50% level, 0.826 at 80% and 0.894 at 90%, so calibration is fair, slightly wide in the centre. Split by posterior sd quartile (cut points 3.4 / 6.2 / 10.4 ft): predicted variance against actual MSE is 5.5 vs 9.3 (lowest half, overconfident), 21.2 vs 21.5, 63.8 vs 67.4, and 238 vs 177 (top 5%, underconfident in variance). Their SSE shares are 15%, 21%, 34% and 29%. An in-sample oracle temperature per spread group improves pooled RMSE only from 5.480 to 5.464 ft (-0.016, below the noise floor). Conclusion: temperature-style recalibration of band weights is not a lever. Moving mass to the correct band needs new evidence.
where_to_use: (a) As a closed question: record that the whole mode-seeking decode family, plus L1/median, top-k and global or spread-conditioned temperature, is measured and rejected for pooled RMSE on our posteriors, so nobody spends GPU time on it. (b) On the training side: the ADL/SMWA finding that the distribution-shaped loss matters more than the decoder suggests trying a distance-aware proper scoring rule (our dormant 'CDF' ranked-probability loss, i.e. discrete CRPS) alongside the alignment cross-entropy. Unlike cross-entropy, it penalises mass on a far-away wrong band more than mass on a near one, which is what squared error cares about. (c) As a proposal generator: SMD-Nets-style K = 2 mixture outputs feeding a reranker or gate (B04), where the mixture mean pi1*mu1 + pi2*mu2 stays RMSE-consistent as the fallback. (d) Monitoring: use per-column posterior sd and multimodality as the confidence signal for B02-style prior fusion.
error_mode_targeted: Band confusion (wrong_mode, blend, multimodal_miss; about 51% of SSE): the decoders make it worse, and a CRPS-style loss may reduce it slightly. Broad or skewed humps (about 13%): the CRPS loss sharpens them in a distance-aware way.
gap_vs_our_implementation: Already done or already known: expectation decode, which is Bayes-optimal for RMSE under calibration and confirmed empirically here. Cross-entropy to a Gaussian-smoothed target (sigma 1.25 levels), which is exactly the SMWA/Chen 2019 recommendation, plus Huber on the expectation, the L2-risk analogue of Stereo Risk's end-to-end risk training. A DME-like 'dominant_mode' decode, which posterior_analysis.py already measures (6.06 ft against 5.47). An AcfNet-style learned-width unimodal target (arch_v1_unimodal, rejected, +0.162 ft at 60 epochs). The literature is consistent with that rejection: forcing unimodality is the opposite of ADL, whose gain comes from letting targets be multimodal. Not done: (1) The measured sweep of top-k, SMWA, median/L1-risk and temperature. This item did it: all are worse or neutral. (2) A distance-aware proper scoring rule. The 'CDF' (ranked-probability) loss exists in seq_NN_train.py (masked_typewell_cdf_loss) but has weight 0.0 in every recipe. (3) A mixture-density or K-hypothesis head (SMD-Nets) that exposes the two band candidates explicitly for a reranker. (4) An ADL-style multimodal target has no clean analogue. Our ground truth is a single TVT per column, and neighbour-column clustering only matters at faults. It would teach the network to put mass on aliases the label rules out, so it should not be adopted.
proposed_experiment: E0 (done in this research, zero cost): decode sweep on results/baseline_check_posterior_all/posterior_all.npz. Scripts are in the session scratchpad (decode_probe.py, decode_probe2.py); fold them into posterior_analysis.py as extra columns (median, topk_k, smwa, temp_T) so every future dump reports them. Result: nothing beats the mean. E1, the ranked-probability (CRPS) loss: in experiments/arch/seq_NN_cfg.py create recipe arch_v7_crps = 0801_V2 with unet_loss_weights['CDF'] set to 0.05/3 (arm A) and 0.05*4/3 (arm B), keeping 'alignment' and 'regression' unchanged. This adds to the loss rather than replacing it, which avoids the confound that sank arch_v1_unimodal. First confirm that masked_typewell_cdf_loss receives the same target_probs as the alignment term and the same mask. Warm-start from results/cnx_tiny_ep150 for 40 epochs, with a control fine-tune of the same length at CDF = 0, two seeds per arm. Judge with seq_NN_robust_compare.py plus the posterior_analysis SSE split (expect a reduction in far wrong_mode SSE, possibly at a cost on ok rows). Also rerun decode_probe2 to check the low-sd overconfidence. E2 (optional, only if B04 proceeds): an SMD-style 2-component head alongside the softmax, trained with mixture NLL at a small weight. Its (mu_k, pi_k) become reranker features, and the softmax mean remains the default output.
implementation_effort: E0 done / low (copy into posterior_analysis.py). E1 low: a config-only change once the CDF loss's target and mask wiring is verified. E2 medium: a new head, a loss, and registration in model_modules() / model_named_parameters().
gpu_cost: E0 about 1 minute on CPU. E1 about 1 h per 40-epoch warm-started tiny fine-tune, so about 6 h for 2 arms + control x 2 seeds; or 5 h per arm at 150 epochs from scratch. The CDF loss is a cumsum over 400 levels, a negligible overhead. E2 adds under 1% in parameters and time.
distillation_compatibility: Fully compatible. E1 only changes the training loss of the teacher or student, and the KD target (the teacher softmax) is unchanged. The CRPS term can also be applied between teacher and student CDFs as a distance-aware complement to the KL term. E2 heads can be distilled with a mixture-matching loss or ignored by the student.
error_correlation_with_ours: Decode variants of the same posterior are almost perfectly correlated with the mean decode and strictly worse, so they are useless as blend members. A CRPS-trained model is the same architecture and would correlate at about 0.85 or more with the other ConvNeXt runs, adding seed-style diversity only.
risk: (1) The metric argument is decisive against all mode-seeking decoders: for pooled RMSE with a reasonably calibrated posterior, the mean is optimal, and our measurements confirm it (every alternative is +0.04 to +0.8 ft). (2) The CRPS loss could over-sharpen: a proper scoring rule is still minimised by the true distribution, but at finite data it may trade calibration for sharpness differently from cross-entropy, and the expected effect is small (likely within the ±0.39 ft single-run noise). (3) Global calibration is already near-optimal (a temperature gain of 0.001 ft; per-spread-group oracle 0.016 ft), so any calibration-only approach has a ceiling of a few hundredths of a foot on this model. (4) The oracle best-mode decode (4.27 ft) invites mode-selection schemes, but it uses the label. Without new evidence (neighbour wells, a prefix, a longer MD context), mode selection is the failed geo-pick / gate / continuity story again.
notes: Key takeaway for the team: the stereo 'multimodal decoding' literature solves a different loss. Stereo Risk makes it explicit: the expectation is the L2-risk solution, and moving to the L1 median helps EPE. Our metric is L2, so we are already at their L2 optimum. The measured numbers on our own posteriors settle it: mean 5.480; T=0.85 5.478; top-64 5.517; median 5.636; top-8 5.946; DME-like dominant mode 6.061; argmax 6.274; SMWA 6.282. The ADL ablation shows the loss mattered more than the decoder (multimodal + SME 0.80 against unimodal + DME 0.82). That points our effort at training-side changes (a distance-aware CRPS loss, and above all more evidence per column), not decode rules. arch_v1_unimodal's failure is consistent with this literature, since it pushed the opposite way from ADL (forcing unimodality).
